mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP indicates strong economic activity, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate above 6% signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If unemployment exceeds 6% but S&P 500 returns remain positive.

mechanism_narrative: When both industrial production and payroll employment exceed their 12-month averages, it indicates strong economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If both proxies are above average but S&P 500 returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, decreasing federal funds rate stimulates economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If federal funds rate decreases but S&P 500 returns are negative during late-cycle.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation as indicated by CPI leads to negative S&P 500 returns due to potential rate hikes.
failure_condition: If CPI is high but S&P 500 returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: A drop in federal funds rate below 0.5% indicates easing, boosting S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS drops below 0.5% but S&P 500 returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts and retail sales signal strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If both proxies rise but S&P 500 returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: In early recovery, low unemployment signals strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If UNRATE is low in early recovery but S&P 500 returns are negative.
